newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's NFI Foksal wants to trim its portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Poland's NFI Foksal wants to trim its portfolio.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No 10 or Foksal wants to reduce the number of companies in its portfolio to between 15 and 20, the deputy president of the fund said.
"In the future we would like to reduce the number of firms where we have strategic stakes. We plan to have between 15 and 20 large firms," Ireneusz Sitarski told Reuters in an interview.
Sitarski said NFI Foksal, which currently has strategic stakes in 33 firms, wanted to focus on such sectors as chemical industry, industry construction, food processing and fire-proof materials.
He said the fund was also planning to float several of its companies and sell several more.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 medium-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms. @
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been able to exchange each of them for 15 shares, one in each fund.
On Thursday, shares of the funds will start trade on the Warsaw bourse.
